problem_statement: ZBus currently only offers synchronous listeners that run inside the publishing context; there is no way to offload a listener's callback to a separate work-queue context. Add a new kind of observer, the async listener, that is set up like a regular listener but whose callback is scheduled to run in a work queue (the system work queue by default) whenever an observed channel is published or notified. An async listener must receive an exact copy of each published message (never lose a message), the callback runs in the work-queue context rather than the publisher's, multiple messages arriving in a burst must all be delivered (the work item resubmits itself until the message FIFO is drained), and the work queue used for an observer must be changeable at runtime (e.g. to an isolated, named work queue).

verification.reason: The statement describes the feature conceptually but omits the exact public API names (macros, function, Kconfig option, struct) and the callback signature that the hidden tests require to compile and run. All missing items are public interface elements that can be added without dictating the implementation.

problems.detail: The Kconfig option CONFIG_ZBUS_ASYNC_LISTNER is used in prj.conf but the statement never names it.

The macros ZBUS_ASYNC_LISTNER_DEFINE(name, callback) and ZBUS_ASYNC_LISTNER_DEFINE_WITH_ENABLE(name, callback, enabled) are used in the test but the statement only says 'set up like a regular listener' without giving the exact macro names.

The function zbus_async_listener_set_work_queue(const struct zbus_observer *obs, struct k_work_q *queue) is called in the test but the statement only says 'changeable at runtime' without naming the function or its parameters.

The test uses CONTAINER_OF(alis3.work, struct zbus_async_listener_work, work) and accesses async_listener->queue; the struct zbus_async_listener_work and its queue and work fields, as well as the observer's work field, are not mentioned in the statement.

The async listener callback signature is void callback(const struct zbus_channel *chan, const void *message) (takes a message pointer, unlike regular listeners which take only the channel); the statement does not specify this signature.

The test checks that an async listener created with ZBUS_ASYNC_LISTNER_DEFINE_WITH_ENABLE(name, NULL, false) (disabled) receives no messages; the statement does not mention the enabled/disabled behaviour.

leak_check.leak_detail: The parenthetical 'the work item resubmits itself until the message FIFO is drained' hints at an internal implementation mechanism; the remaining added details are public interface elements or required behavior used by the tests.
leak_check.suggested_statement: ZBus currently only offers synchronous listeners that run inside the publishing context; there is no way to offload a listener's callback to a separate work-queue context. Add a new kind of observer, the async listener, that is set up like a regular listener but whose callback is scheduled to run in a work queue (the system work queue by default) whenever an observed channel is published or notified. An async listener must receive an exact copy of each published message (never lose a message), the callback runs in the work-queue context rather than the publisher's, multiple messages arriving in a burst must all be delivered, and the work queue used for an observer must be changeable at runtime (e.g. to an isolated, named work queue). The feature is enabled by the Kconfig option CONFIG_ZBUS_ASYNC_LISTENER. Async listeners are defined with the macros ZBUS_ASYNC_LISTENER_DEFINE(name, callback) for an enabled listener, or ZBUS_ASYNC_LISTENER_DEFINE_WITH_ENABLE(name, callback, enable) for a listener with an explicit initial enabled state. The callback must have the signature void callback(const struct zbus_channel *chan, const void *message). The observer type for async listeners is ZBUS_OBSERVER_ASYNC_LISTENER_TYPE. The work queue can be changed at runtime by calling zbus_async_listener_set_work_queue(const struct zbus_observer *obs, struct k_work_q *queue), which returns 0 on success and an error code on failure. Each async listener's state is stored in a struct zbus_async_listener_work (reachable via the observer's work field), which contains a queue field of type struct k_work_q * holding the current work queue and a work field of type struct k_work for the work item.
